The Carnivores field guide

Before you set off.

Your first safari

Start with the time you have and the wildlife or landscapes you most want to see. Compare the driving time between parks and ask which nights are spent inside or outside each park. Share your arrival and departure plans so the team can account for transfers.

What to pack

Bring layers for early drives, a hat, sun protection, binoculars and a reusable water bottle. Ask about baggage limits if your proposal includes a light aircraft, and check which items your accommodation supplies.

Quotes & payment

Dates, group size, accommodation and the route shape your quote. Ask for park fees, transfers, meals and optional activities to be itemised. Confirm the currency, deposit, balance deadline and cancellation terms directly with Carnivores before paying.

Preparing for a trek

Tell the team about your recent hikes and any previous experience at altitude. Ask about daily walking time, acclimatisation days, guide arrangements, equipment hire and the descent plan before choosing an itinerary.

Before you go

A few good questions.

Can we change one of the suggested itineraries?

Yes. These routes are starting points. Tell the team how many days you have, your interests and preferred accommodation so they can prepare a personalised proposal.

How much does a private safari cost?

Your quote depends on dates, group size, route and accommodation. Include an approximate per-person budget in your enquiry so the team can suggest suitable options. Ask for a full breakdown of inclusions and exclusions.

Can we add time in Zanzibar?

Ask the team to include a beach extension in your proposal, with transfers and accommodation suited to your travel dates.

Is this an instant booking?

No. Your enquiry starts a conversation. A booking requires an agreed proposal, confirmed availability and acceptance of the operator’s current booking terms.
